Player forecasts are well calibrated. On the holdout, predicted buckets landed within about 3 points of actual hit rates. The test used who actually played, so live forecasts will be slightly worse because inactives are unknown in advance.

Game lines show no edge. Closing spread MAE was 9.70 points vs 10.11 for our line, and the fitted weight on our line was about zero. Closing totals: 10.18 vs 10.61. So game sides default to pass.

Prop edges are unproven. Calibration shows the probabilities are honest. It does not show they beat DraftKings, because no historical prop lines were available to test against. The edges here are leads to price-check.

2026 holdout, all markets. Dots near the dashed line mean a forecast of X% hit about X% of the time. Bigger dots hold more forecasts.

Data gaps

  • Prop prices: ESPN's DraftKings feed gives lines and milestone levels but no prices. Moneyline, spread and total prices are real. Prop edges assume -110, and each pick shows a minimum acceptable price.
  • 2026 coverage: man/zone and coverage shells have no free 2026 feed. 2025 charting stands in, labeled every time, and flagged when a head coach changed. Coordinator changes are not tracked.
  • Alignment and routes: 2026 slot/wide alignment and routes run are paid data. Target side, depth and 2025 route targets stand in. Press rate, shadow rate, tackle-vs-edge win rate, and run-scheme splits are left out.
  • Under-pressure splits: team pressure rates are 2026 (PFR). Individual QB pressure splits are 2025. Blitz splits are 2026 (FTN).
  • Injury odds: P(plays) values are assumptions from status and practice, not fitted estimates.

nflverse supplied play-by-play, FTN charting, PFR advanced stats, NGS, snap counts, depth charts and rosters. ESPN supplied the schedule, injuries and DraftKings lines. NWS supplied forecasts.

These are estimates, and no selection is guaranteed. After the games, run review.py to score every forecast (Phase 15).

DraftKings via ESPN, pulled Monday, Nov 16 at 5:00 PM. Sun Nov 15, 9:30 AM ET · FC Bayern Munich Stadium.

TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is ruled out. Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is officially questionable after limited practices (Patriots.com injury report, Nov 13), but Ian Rapoport reported Nov 9 that he was expected to miss the next few weeks, and ESPN says he was not in uniform Friday. Corey Kiner is next up. New England rushing lines are held out until inactives. A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is questionable after three limited practices; Hunter Henry (foot) was limited; Drake Maye (right shoulder) practiced in full (Patriots.com). Sunday update: official inactives are out and the game has kicked off. Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) are ACTIVE; Hunter Henry had no game designation; TreVeyon Henderson (illness) went on IR Saturday (ESPN, Mike Reiss, Nov 14); Tommy DeVito is the No. 2 QB and Behren Morton the inactive emergency third QB; G Ben Brown (knee) is inactive (ESPN inactives, Nov 15). Stevenson returns after the Rapoport report that he would miss weeks, so his workload is uncertain.

Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited all week and has no posted game status yet; Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full; Sione Vaki (ankle) did not practice (Patriots.com injury report, Nov 13). Sunday update: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) and Sione Vaki (ankle) are ACTIVE for Munich (ESPN inactives, Nov 15). Inactive: DT Mekhi Wingo, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, DE Ahmed Hassanein; C Cade Mays and CB D.J. Reed were already out.

Defensive scheme

DET defense vs NE offense: what to attack

  • DET is soft on Inter 10-19 throws to the middle (+1.83 EPA/att vs league +0.58, 17 attempts).
  • DET is soft on Deep 20+ throws to the right (+0.82 EPA/att vs league +0.39, 20 attempts).
  • Avoid Inter 10-19 throws to the left: DET allows -0.50 EPA/att vs league +0.30 (20 attempts).
  • DET gives up 81 yds/game to All TE (league 54).
  • Run stuffed: Outside (tackle / end) gains only 3.4 YPC on DET (league 4.6).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Aidan Hutchinson (DE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Drake Maye and Jared Goff. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Amon-Ra St. Brown 30+ receiving yds (91%) + Jameson Williams 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.2%, fair -497. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.3% vs 75.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Sam LaPorta 20+ receiving yds (80%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 50+ receiving yds (78%) + Jameson Williams 25+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 47.8%, fair +109. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 33.9% vs 34.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jahmyr Gibbs 70+ rushing yds (61%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 70+ receiving yds (60%) + Sam LaPorta 40+ receiving yds (56%). Joint estimate 20.8%, fair +380. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 12.5% vs 12.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Amon-Ra St. Brown 30+ receiving yds (91%) + Jameson Williams 10+ receiving yds (91%). Joint estimate 83.2%, fair -497. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.3% vs 75.4% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Sam LaPorta 20+ receiving yds (80%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 50+ receiving yds (78%) + Jameson Williams 25+ receiving yds (77%). Joint estimate 47.8%, fair +109. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 33.9% vs 34.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Jahmyr Gibbs 70+ rushing yds (61%) + Amon-Ra St. Brown 70+ receiving yds (60%) + Sam LaPorta 40+ receiving yds (56%). Joint estimate 20.8%, fair +380. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 12.5% vs 12.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Patrick Mahomes (right elbow) practiced in full and is in line to start (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13; NFL.com injury report). Josh Downs joined the roster this week after the Colts traded him and has no role history in Kansas City. Sunday update: Kenneth Walker III (groin) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports, Nov 14). Emmett Johnson is the top back (ESPN, citing Adam Schefter, Nov 14); Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is questionable and Nate Carter was elevated from the practice squad. Kansas City rushing lines are held out and any Walker prop is void. Andy Reid said Josh Downs looks ready to play (Nov 13). LT Jaylon Moore (ankle) and DT Peter Woods (neck) are out. Schefter reported Sunday that outside doctors also reviewed Mahomes's elbow scans; he is still in line to start. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' site), so Emmett Johnson leads the backfield with Nate Carter rotating in. Josh Downs is ACTIVE and makes his Chiefs debut after three practices; his workload is unknown. Patrick Mahomes starts with no designation; Garrett Nussmeier is the inactive emergency third QB.

Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has not practiced and is doubtful (ESPN, Nov 11; NFL.com injury report). Sunday update: Branch was downgraded to OUT Friday; LB Divine Deablo (forearm) was downgraded to out Saturday (ESPN, citing Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' site, Nov 14). Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Zachariah Branch is inactive. Michael Penix Jr. starts; Andy Dalton is the inactive emergency third QB, so Tua Tagovailoa is the backup.

KC: Patrick Mahomes (right elbow) practiced in full and is in line to start (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13; NFL.com injury report). Josh Downs joined the roster this week after the Colts traded him and has no role history in Kansas City. Sunday update: Kenneth Walker III (groin) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports, Nov 14). Emmett Johnson is the top back (ESPN, citing Adam Schefter, Nov 14); Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is questionable and Nate Carter was elevated from the practice squad. Kansas City rushing lines are held out and any Walker prop is void. Andy Reid said Josh Downs looks ready to play (Nov 13). LT Jaylon Moore (ankle) and DT Peter Woods (neck) are out. Schefter reported Sunday that outside doctors also reviewed Mahomes's elbow scans; he is still in line to start. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' site), so Emmett Johnson leads the backfield with Nate Carter rotating in. Josh Downs is ACTIVE and makes his Chiefs debut after three practices; his workload is unknown. Patrick Mahomes starts with no designation; Garrett Nussmeier is the inactive emergency third QB.

Patrick Mahomes (right elbow) practiced in full and is in line to start (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13; NFL.com injury report). Josh Downs joined the roster this week after the Colts traded him and has no role history in Kansas City. Sunday update: Kenneth Walker III (groin) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports, Nov 14). Emmett Johnson is the top back (ESPN, citing Adam Schefter, Nov 14); Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is questionable and Nate Carter was elevated from the practice squad. Kansas City rushing lines are held out and any Walker prop is void. Andy Reid said Josh Downs looks ready to play (Nov 13). LT Jaylon Moore (ankle) and DT Peter Woods (neck) are out. Schefter reported Sunday that outside doctors also reviewed Mahomes's elbow scans; he is still in line to start. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' site), so Emmett Johnson leads the backfield with Nate Carter rotating in. Josh Downs is ACTIVE and makes his Chiefs debut after three practices; his workload is unknown. Patrick Mahomes starts with no designation; Garrett Nussmeier is the inactive emergency third QB.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Jaydn Ott (RB, Questionable), Mansoor Delane (CB, Questionable), Josh Woods (LB, Questionable), James Pearce Jr. (LB, Questionable), Gervon Dexter Sr. (DT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Patrick Mahomes and Michael Penix Jr.. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Drake London 25+ receiving yds (88%) + Bijan Robinson 40+ rushing yds (87%). Joint estimate 76.8%, fair -331. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 69.1% vs 69.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Kyle Pitts 10+ receiving yds (79%) + Bijan Robinson 50+ rushing yds (79%) + Drake London 40+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 47.0%, fair +113. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 34.8% vs 34.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Kyle Pitts 20+ receiving yds (61%) + Bijan Robinson 70+ rushing yds (58%) + Michael Penix Jr. 190+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 25.4%, fair +294. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 16.9% vs 13.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Drake London 25+ receiving yds (88%) + Bijan Robinson 40+ rushing yds (87%). Joint estimate 76.8%, fair -331. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 69.1% vs 69.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Kyle Pitts 10+ receiving yds (79%) + Bijan Robinson 50+ rushing yds (79%) + Drake London 40+ receiving yds (75%). Joint estimate 47.0%, fair +113. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 34.8% vs 34.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Kyle Pitts 20+ receiving yds (61%) + Bijan Robinson 70+ rushing yds (58%) + Michael Penix Jr. 190+ passing yds (57%). Joint estimate 25.4%, fair +294. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 16.9% vs 13.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Patrick Mahomes (right elbow) practiced in full and is in line to start (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13; NFL.com injury report). Josh Downs joined the roster this week after the Colts traded him and has no role history in Kansas City. Sunday update: Kenneth Walker III (groin) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports, Nov 14). Emmett Johnson is the top back (ESPN, citing Adam Schefter, Nov 14); Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is questionable and Nate Carter was elevated from the practice squad. Kansas City rushing lines are held out and any Walker prop is void. Andy Reid said Josh Downs looks ready to play (Nov 13). LT Jaylon Moore (ankle) and DT Peter Woods (neck) are out. Schefter reported Sunday that outside doctors also reviewed Mahomes's elbow scans; he is still in line to start. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jaydn Ott (hamstring) is RULED OUT (ESPN, citing Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' site), so Emmett Johnson leads the backfield with Nate Carter rotating in. Josh Downs is ACTIVE and makes his Chiefs debut after three practices; his workload is unknown. Patrick Mahomes starts with no designation; Garrett Nussmeier is the inactive emergency third QB.

Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has not practiced and is doubtful (ESPN, Nov 11; NFL.com injury report). Sunday update: Branch was downgraded to OUT Friday; LB Divine Deablo (forearm) was downgraded to out Saturday (ESPN, citing Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' site, Nov 14). Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Zachariah Branch is inactive. Michael Penix Jr. starts; Andy Dalton is the inactive emergency third QB, so Tua Tagovailoa is the backup.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Kenneth Walker III (RB, Out); Jaylon Moore (OT, Out); Peter Woods (DT, Out); Jaydn Ott (RB, Questionable); Mansoor Delane (CB, Questionable); Divine Deablo (LB, Out); Zachariah Branch (WR, Out); Josh Woods (LB, Questionable); James Pearce Jr. (LB, Questionable); Gervon Dexter Sr. (DT, Questionable).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Will Anderson Jr. (DE, Questionable), Jake Hummel (LB, Questionable), Braden Smith (OT, Questionable), Denzel Boston (WR, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: C.J. Stroud and Deshaun Watson. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Harold Fannin Jr. 10+ receiving yds (89%) + Quinshon Judkins 15+ rushing yds (89%). Joint estimate 80.1%, fair -402. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 73.1% vs 73.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Deshaun Watson 170+ passing yds (78%) + Harold Fannin Jr. 20+ receiving yds (77%) + Quinshon Judkins 25+ rushing yds (74%). Joint estimate 49.6%, fair +102. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 37.8% vs 33.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Deshaun Watson 200+ passing yds (60%) + KC Concepcion 30+ receiving yds (58%) + Jerry Jeudy 15+ receiving yds (58%). Joint estimate 28.1%, fair +255. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 19.3% vs 13.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

DraftKings via ESPN, pulled Monday, Nov 16 at 5:00 PM. Sun Nov 15, 1:00 PM ET · Lambeau Field.

Kirk Cousins, acquired from the Raiders on Nov 10, is expected to start at Green Bay (ESPN injury page, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13); the team has not been quoted naming him, but the depth chart lists him first. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is doubtful and week-to-week, and Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited Thursday. T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12-13). Cousins's 2026 history is with Las Vegas and he has had one week in this offense, so Minnesota passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Sunday update: Kirk Cousins is confirmed as the starter; Carson Wentz has no designation and backs him up (ESPN, Nov 13). Kyler Murray is out, with the team targeting Nov 29 (ESPN, citing Tom Pelissero, Nov 14). T.J. Hockenson (wrist) and Jauan Jennings (calf) are RULED OUT (ESPN, Nov 13). Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable and a game-time decision (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 15). LB Blake Cashman (concussion) is out. TE Devin Culp and WR Jeshaun Jones were elevated. Any Hockenson prop is void. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jordan Addison (thumb) is INACTIVE after a pregame workout (ESPN, citing Tom Pelissero); with Hockenson and Jennings also inactive, Justin Jefferson is the only regular target left, so any Addison prop is void. Kirk Cousins starts; Max Brosmer is the inactive QB. The model has no Minnesota history for Cousins and projects Carson Wentz as the passer, so Minnesota passing lines are not usable and any Wentz prop is void.

Josh Jacobs (broken finger) is out; he has surgery Friday and is expected to miss multiple weeks (Packers.com, Nov 9; ESPN, citing Matt Schneidman, Nov 12). Kaleb Johnson led the backfield with 14 carries in Week 9, and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is off the injury report (ESPN, Nov 10-11). Roles are changing, so Green Bay rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Jacobs had surgery Friday and is out. RB Chris Brooks (ankle) and WR Skyy Moore (ankle) were activated from IR Saturday and are questionable; TE Josh Whyle (concussion) went on IR; Savion Williams (groin) has no designation (ESPN, Nov 13-14). Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Pierre Strong Jr. is a healthy scratch. Chris Brooks and Skyy Moore are ACTIVE (ESPN, citing Mike Spofford of the Packers' site). ESPN lists MarShawn Lloyd as the starter with Brooks and Kaleb Johnson in reserve, so the hold on Green Bay rushing lines stays. Guards Kevin Zeitler and Sean Rhyan (ankles) and LB Zaire Franklin (shin) are inactive.

Kirk Cousins, acquired from the Raiders on Nov 10, is expected to start at Green Bay (ESPN injury page, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13); the team has not been quoted naming him, but the depth chart lists him first. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is doubtful and week-to-week, and Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited Thursday. T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12-13). Cousins's 2026 history is with Las Vegas and he has had one week in this offense, so Minnesota passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Sunday update: Kirk Cousins is confirmed as the starter; Carson Wentz has no designation and backs him up (ESPN, Nov 13). Kyler Murray is out, with the team targeting Nov 29 (ESPN, citing Tom Pelissero, Nov 14). T.J. Hockenson (wrist) and Jauan Jennings (calf) are RULED OUT (ESPN, Nov 13). Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable and a game-time decision (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 15). LB Blake Cashman (concussion) is out. TE Devin Culp and WR Jeshaun Jones were elevated. Any Hockenson prop is void. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jordan Addison (thumb) is INACTIVE after a pregame workout (ESPN, citing Tom Pelissero); with Hockenson and Jennings also inactive, Justin Jefferson is the only regular target left, so any Addison prop is void. Kirk Cousins starts; Max Brosmer is the inactive QB. The model has no Minnesota history for Cousins and projects Carson Wentz as the passer, so Minnesota passing lines are not usable and any Wentz prop is void.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Jordan Addison (WR, Questionable), Joshua Metellus (S, Questionable), Chris Brooks (RB, Questionable), Skyy Moore (WR, Questionable), Kevin Zeitler (G, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Carson Wentz and Jordan Love. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Aaron Jones 15+ rushing yds (89%) + Matthew Golden 20+ receiving yds (88%). Joint estimate 78.2%, fair -359. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 70.7% vs 70.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Matthew Golden 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Christian Watson 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Jordan Mason 20+ rushing yds (79%). Joint estimate 49.7%, fair +101. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 37.5% vs 37.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tucker Kraft 20+ receiving yds (62%) + Jordan Love 210+ passing yds (62%) + Christian Watson 50+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 34.4%, fair +190. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.3% vs 14.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Aaron Jones 15+ rushing yds (89%) + Matthew Golden 20+ receiving yds (88%). Joint estimate 78.2%, fair -359. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 70.7% vs 70.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Matthew Golden 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Christian Watson 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Jordan Mason 20+ rushing yds (79%). Joint estimate 49.7%, fair +101. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 37.5% vs 37.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tucker Kraft 20+ receiving yds (62%) + Jordan Love 210+ passing yds (62%) + Christian Watson 50+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 34.4%, fair +190. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.3% vs 14.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

GB strengths: explosive passing on offense (#4); explosive passing on defense (#6). Weaknesses: rushing EPA on offense (#32); explosive runs on offense (#28); success rate on offense (#27).

Kirk Cousins, acquired from the Raiders on Nov 10, is expected to start at Green Bay (ESPN injury page, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 13); the team has not been quoted naming him, but the depth chart lists him first. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is doubtful and week-to-week, and Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited Thursday. T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12-13). Cousins's 2026 history is with Las Vegas and he has had one week in this offense, so Minnesota passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Sunday update: Kirk Cousins is confirmed as the starter; Carson Wentz has no designation and backs him up (ESPN, Nov 13). Kyler Murray is out, with the team targeting Nov 29 (ESPN, citing Tom Pelissero, Nov 14). T.J. Hockenson (wrist) and Jauan Jennings (calf) are RULED OUT (ESPN, Nov 13). Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable and a game-time decision (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 15). LB Blake Cashman (concussion) is out. TE Devin Culp and WR Jeshaun Jones were elevated. Any Hockenson prop is void. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Jordan Addison (thumb) is INACTIVE after a pregame workout (ESPN, citing Tom Pelissero); with Hockenson and Jennings also inactive, Justin Jefferson is the only regular target left, so any Addison prop is void. Kirk Cousins starts; Max Brosmer is the inactive QB. The model has no Minnesota history for Cousins and projects Carson Wentz as the passer, so Minnesota passing lines are not usable and any Wentz prop is void.

Josh Jacobs (broken finger) is out; he has surgery Friday and is expected to miss multiple weeks (Packers.com, Nov 9; ESPN, citing Matt Schneidman, Nov 12). Kaleb Johnson led the backfield with 14 carries in Week 9, and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is off the injury report (ESPN, Nov 10-11). Roles are changing, so Green Bay rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Jacobs had surgery Friday and is out. RB Chris Brooks (ankle) and WR Skyy Moore (ankle) were activated from IR Saturday and are questionable; TE Josh Whyle (concussion) went on IR; Savion Williams (groin) has no designation (ESPN, Nov 13-14). Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Pierre Strong Jr. is a healthy scratch. Chris Brooks and Skyy Moore are ACTIVE (ESPN, citing Mike Spofford of the Packers' site). ESPN lists MarShawn Lloyd as the starter with Brooks and Kaleb Johnson in reserve, so the hold on Green Bay rushing lines stays. Guards Kevin Zeitler and Sean Rhyan (ankles) and LB Zaire Franklin (shin) are inactive.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Jordan Addison (WR, Questionable); Kyler Murray (QB, Out); Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (DE, Out); Joshua Metellus (S, Questionable); Blake Cashman (LB, Out); Chris Brooks (RB, Questionable); Skyy Moore (WR, Questionable); Josh Jacobs (RB, Out); Kevin Zeitler (G, Questionable).

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

3 · Traps

No line here pairs a popular read with a model that disagrees.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Tyjae Spears (RB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Trevor Lawrence and Cam Ward. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Parker Washington 10+ receiving yds (94%) + Trevor Lawrence 160+ passing yds (92%). Joint estimate 88.2%, fair -748. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 81.8% vs 79.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Parker Washington 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Jakobi Meyers 25+ receiving yds (78%) + Trevor Lawrence 210+ passing yds (77%). Joint estimate 57.7%, fair -136. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 42.4% vs 34.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Chris Rodriguez Jr. 20+ rushing yds (62%) + Parker Washington 50+ receiving yds (61%) + Jakobi Meyers 42+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 23.1%, fair +332. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 14.2% vs 14.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Kyle McCord makes his first NFL start; Malik Willis (core muscle) went on IR Nov 10 and misses at least four games (ESPN, citing Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network, Nov 10). Miami passing history under Willis is stale, so its passing and receiving lines are low confidence. WR Chris Bell (knee) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12). Sunday update: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful and Jared Wayne (quad) is ruled out; Will Kacmarek has no designation. QB Brady Cook and WR Jalen Reagor were elevated from the practice squad (ESPN, citing the Sun Sentinel, Nov 13-14). C Aaron Brewer is out. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Chris Bell (knee) is INACTIVE, along with Jared Wayne and TE Justin Joly (healthy scratch). ESPN expects Kevin Coleman Jr. and Jalen Tolbert to share the No. 3 receiver snaps. Kyle McCord starts with Brady Cook behind him.

The Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Nov 10 and Alec Pierce (heel) is on IR. Coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould takes the slot and Deion Burks and Ashton Dulin step into larger roles (ESPN, Stephen Holder, Nov 11). Indianapolis receiving lines carry role uncertainty. Sunday update: TE Mo Alie-Cox (groin) went on IR and TE Will Mallory (hamstring) was downgraded to OUT Saturday, leaving Tyler Warren as the main tight end; WR Quez Watkins was elevated; OT Jalen Travis (knee) is out (ESPN, Nov 14). Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Will Mallory is out as expected; Riley Leonard is the inactive emergency third QB and Daniel Jones starts.

Model's IND passing game for this matchup: Daniel Jones 192 pass yards, 2.3 sacks; Tyler Warren 46 rec yds, Laquon Treadwell 22 rec yds, Ashton Dulin 14 rec yds. These already include each defense's sack rate; the pressure matchup itself is not added (see the backtest below).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Chris Bell (WR, Doubtful).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: None and Daniel Jones. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

MIA strengths: none in the top 7. Weaknesses: success rate on defense (#30); success rate on offense (#29); 3rd downs on defense (#28); passing EPA on defense (#28); overall EPA on defense (#27).

IND strengths: 3rd downs on defense (#5). Weaknesses: rushing EPA on defense (#32); explosive passing on defense (#31); explosive passing on offense (#30); overall EPA on offense (#30); passing EPA on offense (#30).

Kyle McCord makes his first NFL start; Malik Willis (core muscle) went on IR Nov 10 and misses at least four games (ESPN, citing Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network, Nov 10). Miami passing history under Willis is stale, so its passing and receiving lines are low confidence. WR Chris Bell (knee) did not practice Thursday (ESPN, Nov 12). Sunday update: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful and Jared Wayne (quad) is ruled out; Will Kacmarek has no designation. QB Brady Cook and WR Jalen Reagor were elevated from the practice squad (ESPN, citing the Sun Sentinel, Nov 13-14). C Aaron Brewer is out. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Chris Bell (knee) is INACTIVE, along with Jared Wayne and TE Justin Joly (healthy scratch). ESPN expects Kevin Coleman Jr. and Jalen Tolbert to share the No. 3 receiver snaps. Kyle McCord starts with Brady Cook behind him.

The Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Nov 10 and Alec Pierce (heel) is on IR. Coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould takes the slot and Deion Burks and Ashton Dulin step into larger roles (ESPN, Stephen Holder, Nov 11). Indianapolis receiving lines carry role uncertainty. Sunday update: TE Mo Alie-Cox (groin) went on IR and TE Will Mallory (hamstring) was downgraded to OUT Saturday, leaving Tyler Warren as the main tight end; WR Quez Watkins was elevated; OT Jalen Travis (knee) is out (ESPN, Nov 14). Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Will Mallory is out as expected; Riley Leonard is the inactive emergency third QB and Daniel Jones starts.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Darrell Baker Jr. (CB, Out); Aaron Brewer (C, Out); Jared Wayne (WR, Out); Chris Bell (WR, Doubtful); Will Mallory (TE, Out); Jalen Travis (OT, Out); Jaylon Carlies (LB, Out).

CJ Donaldson, C Erik McCoy and RT Taliese Fuaga are inactive.

NO QB vs CAR rush

Alvin Kamara (rest/back) practiced in full Thursday. Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is still on IR but was limited in practice, and CJ Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice (ESPN, citing WWL-TV, Nov 12). Audric Estime led the backfield with 15 carries in Week 9; if Etienne is activated the roles change. Sunday update: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) was ACTIVATED from IR Saturday and is questionable (ESPN, citing Nick Underhill, Nov 14); his first game back makes the Kamara/Estime/Etienne split unknown, so New Orleans rushing lines are held out. CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is ruled out. C Erik McCoy (biceps) and RT Taliese Fuaga (knee) are out, which hurts pass protection. Inactives update (ESPN injury feed and ESPN inactives report, Nov 15, about 11:40 AM ET): Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is ACTIVE, his first game since Week 3; ESPN expects him back in a lead role with a possibly managed workload, so the hold on New Orleans rushing lines stays. CJ Donaldson, C Erik McCoy and RT Taliese Fuaga are inactive.

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Jaelan Phillips (LB, Questionable), Xavier Legette (WR, Questionable), Travis Etienne Jr. (RB, Questionable), Martin Emerson Jr. (CB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Bryce Young and Tyler Shough. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Tetairoa McMillan 15+ receiving yds (92%) + Bryce Young 170+ passing yds (90%). Joint estimate 85.8%, fair -606. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 78.6% vs 76.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Darren Waller 10+ receiving yds (78%) + Jalen Coker 20+ receiving yds (78%) + Bryce Young 210+ passing yds (76%). Joint estimate 53.0%, fair -113. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.5% vs 36.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tetairoa McMillan 50+ receiving yds (62%) + Bryce Young 240+ passing yds (61%) + Tommy Tremble 10+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 31.2%, fair +220. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.8% vs 15.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Balanced: Darren Waller 10+ receiving yds (78%) + Jalen Coker 20+ receiving yds (78%) + Bryce Young 210+ passing yds (76%). Joint estimate 53.0%, fair -113. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.5% vs 36.2% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Tetairoa McMillan 50+ receiving yds (62%) + Bryce Young 240+ passing yds (61%) + Tommy Tremble 10+ receiving yds (60%). Joint estimate 31.2%, fair +220. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.8% vs 15.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Jordan Hancock (CB, Questionable), Spencer Brown (OT, Doubtful), Christian Benford (CB, Questionable), Sam Franklin Jr. (S, Questionable), Garrett Wilson (WR, Questionable), VJ Payne (S, Questionable), Adonai Mitchell (WR, Questionable), Omar Cooper Jr. (WR, Questionable), Nahshon Wright (CB, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Josh Allen and Geno Smith. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Josh Allen 160+ passing yds (91%) + Dalton Kincaid 10+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 83.6%, fair -510. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.4% vs 73.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Adonai Mitchell 10+ receiving yds (80%) + Keon Coleman 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Josh Allen 200+ passing yds (79%). Joint estimate 54.3%, fair -119. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.6% vs 37.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Josh Allen 240+ passing yds (62%) + Ty Johnson 10+ receiving yds (61%) + Keon Coleman 30+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 31.1%, fair +221. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.7% vs 16.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Balanced: Adonai Mitchell 10+ receiving yds (80%) + Keon Coleman 15+ receiving yds (79%) + Josh Allen 200+ passing yds (79%). Joint estimate 54.3%, fair -119. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 40.6% vs 37.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Josh Allen 240+ passing yds (62%) + Ty Johnson 10+ receiving yds (61%) + Keon Coleman 30+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 31.1%, fair +221. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 21.7% vs 16.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Sam Darnold (quad) is out again and coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas (ESPN/ABC7 and Fox 13 Seattle, Nov 9; ESPN injury page, Nov 10). The depth-chart feed still lists Darnold. Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited Thursday (ESPN, citing John Boyle of Seahawks.com, Nov 13), so if he can't go Jalen Milroe would make his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample. In the backfield, Zach Charbonnet took 16 carries and Jadarian Price 9 in Week 9 while Emanuel Wilson did not play a snap (ESPN, Nov 9-11). The carry-share history still credits Wilson, so Seattle rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Drew Lock has no injury designation and starts (ESPN, Brady Henderson, Nov 13). LT Charles Cross (ankle), G Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (shoulder) are ruled out (ESPN, citing John Boyle, Nov 14); two line starters missing raises Lock's pressure risk.

Rookie Fernando Mendoza makes his first NFL start after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Nov 10 (ESPN, Adam Schefter, Nov 10); Aidan O'Connell is the backup (ESPN, citing The Athletic, Nov 11). Mendoza has no NFL passing sample, so Las Vegas passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Sunday update: WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. (back) is questionable; TE Carter Runyon was elevated (ESPN, Nov 14).

Adjusted ratings are opponent-adjusted points per game; rank 1 is best. The sim centers on the market, so implied points carry the most weight. SEA: Sam Darnold (quad) is out again and coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas (ESPN/ABC7 and Fox 13 Seattle, Nov 9; ESPN injury page, Nov 10). The depth-chart feed still lists Darnold. Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited Thursday (ESPN, citing John Boyle of Seahawks.com, Nov 13), so if he can't go Jalen Milroe would make his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample. In the backfield, Zach Charbonnet took 16 carries and Jadarian Price 9 in Week 9 while Emanuel Wilson did not play a snap (ESPN, Nov 9-11). The carry-share history still credits Wilson, so Seattle rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Drew Lock has no injury designation and starts (ESPN, Brady Henderson, Nov 13). LT Charles Cross (ankle), G Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (shoulder) are ruled out (ESPN, citing John Boyle, Nov 14); two line starters missing raises Lock's pressure risk. LV: Rookie Fernando Mendoza makes his first NFL start after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Nov 10 (ESPN, Adam Schefter, Nov 10); Aidan O'Connell is the backup (ESPN, citing The Athletic, Nov 11). Mendoza has no NFL passing sample, so Las Vegas passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Sunday update: WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. (back) is questionable; TE Carter Runyon was elevated (ESPN, Nov 14).

Defensive scheme

LV defense vs SEA offense: what to attack

  • LV is soft on Inter 10-19 throws to the middle (+1.17 EPA/att vs league +0.58, 18 attempts).
  • LV is soft on Deep 20+ throws to the left (+0.95 EPA/att vs league +0.36, 19 attempts).
  • Avoid Deep 20+ throws to the right: LV allows +0.08 EPA/att vs league +0.39 (19 attempts).
  • Pressure mismatch favors LV: its 24% pressure rate meets a SEA line allowing 24% (league 21%).
  • LV gives up 61 yds/game to WR2 (league 41).
  • Run lane: Inside (middle / guard) gains 4.6 YPC on LV (league 3.8).
  • Run lane: Outside (tackle / end) gains 5.9 YPC on LV (league 4.6).

SEA QB vs LV rush

Sam Darnold (quad) is out again and coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas (ESPN/ABC7 and Fox 13 Seattle, Nov 9; ESPN injury page, Nov 10). The depth-chart feed still lists Darnold. Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited Thursday (ESPN, citing John Boyle of Seahawks.com, Nov 13), so if he can't go Jalen Milroe would make his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample. In the backfield, Zach Charbonnet took 16 carries and Jadarian Price 9 in Week 9 while Emanuel Wilson did not play a snap (ESPN, Nov 9-11). The carry-share history still credits Wilson, so Seattle rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Drew Lock has no injury designation and starts (ESPN, Brady Henderson, Nov 13). LT Charles Cross (ankle), G Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (shoulder) are ruled out (ESPN, citing John Boyle, Nov 14); two line starters missing raises Lock's pressure risk.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Thomas Booker IV (DT, Questionable), Dont'e Thornton Jr. (WR, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Drew Lock and Fernando Mendoza. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Ashton Jeanty 15+ rushing yds (83%) + Mike Washington Jr. 15+ rushing yds (81%). Joint estimate 67.9%, fair -211. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 61.1% vs 60.5% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

SEA strengths: explosive passing on defense (#2); explosive runs on defense (#2); success rate on defense (#2); 3rd downs on defense (#4); passing EPA on defense (#4). Weaknesses: red-zone TDs on defense (#28); rushing EPA on offense (#27).

LV strengths: 3rd downs on offense (#6). Weaknesses: explosive runs on offense (#32); success rate on defense (#32); 3rd downs on defense (#31); rushing EPA on offense (#31); overall EPA on defense (#30).

Sam Darnold (quad) is out again and coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas (ESPN/ABC7 and Fox 13 Seattle, Nov 9; ESPN injury page, Nov 10). The depth-chart feed still lists Darnold. Lock (right elbow/oblique) was limited Thursday (ESPN, citing John Boyle of Seahawks.com, Nov 13), so if he can't go Jalen Milroe would make his first NFL start. Seattle passing and receiving lines rest on Lock's small 2026 sample. In the backfield, Zach Charbonnet took 16 carries and Jadarian Price 9 in Week 9 while Emanuel Wilson did not play a snap (ESPN, Nov 9-11). The carry-share history still credits Wilson, so Seattle rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Drew Lock has no injury designation and starts (ESPN, Brady Henderson, Nov 13). LT Charles Cross (ankle), G Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (shoulder) are ruled out (ESPN, citing John Boyle, Nov 14); two line starters missing raises Lock's pressure risk.

Rookie Fernando Mendoza makes his first NFL start after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Nov 10 (ESPN, Adam Schefter, Nov 10); Aidan O'Connell is the backup (ESPN, citing The Athletic, Nov 11). Mendoza has no NFL passing sample, so Las Vegas passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Sunday update: WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. (back) is questionable; TE Carter Runyon was elevated (ESPN, Nov 14).

Key injuries and uncertainties: Quenton Nelson (G, Out); Charles Cross (OT, Out); Leonard Williams (DT, Out); Sam Darnold (QB, Out); Thomas Booker IV (DT, Questionable); Dont'e Thornton Jr. (WR, Questionable).

DraftKings via ESPN, pulled Monday, Nov 16 at 5:00 PM. Sun Nov 15, 4:05 PM ET · State Farm Stadium.

Puka Nacua (MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe) went on IR Thursday and misses at least four games (ESPN injury page, Nov 13; TheRams.com). Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) are also on IR. Tight ends Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice and Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited (ESPN, citing Adam Caplan, Nov 13). Nacua's targets have to be redistributed, so Rams passing and receiving lines carry role uncertainty. Sunday update: Tyler Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) are cleared with no designation; Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable (ESPN, Sarah Barshop, Nov 13). Sean McVay said CJ Daniels will play more, and Konata Mumpfield takes a larger role. G Steve Avila (hamstring) is out.

Rookie Carson Beck makes his first NFL start; coach Mike LaFleur confirmed it Wednesday (ESPN, citing Darren Urban of the Cardinals' site, Nov 11). Gardner Minshew (elbow, IR) is out for the season, and WRs Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are on IR (ESPN). Arizona passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Backfield: Jeremiyah Love and James Conner remain on IR, and Conner won't return this week (ESPN). Bam Knight (concussion) missed Week 9, when Tyler Allgeier took 17 carries; Knight practiced in full Thursday and is listed questionable (ESPN, citing the Cardinals' site, Nov 13). Arizona rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Bam Knight was cleared from the concussion protocol and plays (ESPN, Josh Weinfuss, Nov 13), so he and Allgeier share the backfield. TE Hunter Long (knee) was activated from IR and is questionable; WR Zay Jones was elevated; Reggie Virgil and Simi Fehoko take larger roles (ESPN, citing the Cardinals' site, Nov 13-14). G Jon Gaines II (ankle) is out.

Quarterback vs pass rush

LA QB vs ARI rush

Puka Nacua (MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe) went on IR Thursday and misses at least four games (ESPN injury page, Nov 13; TheRams.com). Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) are also on IR. Tight ends Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice and Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited (ESPN, citing Adam Caplan, Nov 13). Nacua's targets have to be redistributed, so Rams passing and receiving lines carry role uncertainty. Sunday update: Tyler Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) are cleared with no designation; Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable (ESPN, Sarah Barshop, Nov 13). Sean McVay said CJ Daniels will play more, and Konata Mumpfield takes a larger role. G Steve Avila (hamstring) is out.

Matthew Stafford: 385 dropbacks in 2026, +0.09 EPA/db, CPOE 0.4, time to throw 2.70s, intended air yards 7.6, sack rate 3.9%, turnover-worthy throws 3.8%. Pressure-to-sack rate in 2025: 15.4%. 2026 under-pressure splits are not free, so 2025 stands in and blitz splits come from 2026 charting.

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Trent McDuffie (CB, Questionable), Kam Curl (S, Questionable), Davis Allen (TE, Questionable), Myles Garrett (DE, Questionable), Hunter Long (TE, Questionable), Jayden Williams (OT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Matthew Stafford and None. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Balanced: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive: not enough legs at this risk level with a posted milestone.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

LA strengths: 3rd downs on defense (#2); rushing EPA on defense (#2); overall EPA on defense (#3); passing EPA on defense (#3); red-zone TDs on defense (#4). Weaknesses: none in the bottom 7.

ARI strengths: none in the top 7. Weaknesses: passing EPA on defense (#32); explosive passing on offense (#31); overall EPA on defense (#31); red-zone TDs on offense (#30); red-zone TDs on defense (#27).

Puka Nacua (MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe) went on IR Thursday and misses at least four games (ESPN injury page, Nov 13; TheRams.com). Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) are also on IR. Tight ends Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice and Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited (ESPN, citing Adam Caplan, Nov 13). Nacua's targets have to be redistributed, so Rams passing and receiving lines carry role uncertainty. Sunday update: Tyler Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) are cleared with no designation; Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable (ESPN, Sarah Barshop, Nov 13). Sean McVay said CJ Daniels will play more, and Konata Mumpfield takes a larger role. G Steve Avila (hamstring) is out.

Rookie Carson Beck makes his first NFL start; coach Mike LaFleur confirmed it Wednesday (ESPN, citing Darren Urban of the Cardinals' site, Nov 11). Gardner Minshew (elbow, IR) is out for the season, and WRs Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are on IR (ESPN). Arizona passing and receiving lines are low confidence. Backfield: Jeremiyah Love and James Conner remain on IR, and Conner won't return this week (ESPN). Bam Knight (concussion) missed Week 9, when Tyler Allgeier took 17 carries; Knight practiced in full Thursday and is listed questionable (ESPN, citing the Cardinals' site, Nov 13). Arizona rushing lines are held out. Sunday update: Bam Knight was cleared from the concussion protocol and plays (ESPN, Josh Weinfuss, Nov 13), so he and Allgeier share the backfield. TE Hunter Long (knee) was activated from IR and is questionable; WR Zay Jones was elevated; Reggie Virgil and Simi Fehoko take larger roles (ESPN, citing the Cardinals' site, Nov 13-14). G Jon Gaines II (ankle) is out.

Key injuries and uncertainties: Steve Avila (G, Out); Trent McDuffie (CB, Questionable); Kam Curl (S, Questionable); Davis Allen (TE, Questionable); Myles Garrett (DE, Questionable); Hunter Long (TE, Questionable); Jayden Williams (OT, Questionable); Jon Gaines II (G, Out).

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Trent Williams (OT, Questionable), Renardo Green (CB, Questionable), Joey Porter Jr. (CB, Questionable), DaRon Bland (CB, Questionable), Jonathan Bullard (DT, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Brock Purdy and Dak Prescott. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: George Pickens 10+ receiving yds (95%) + Javonte Williams 30+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 87.9%, fair -725. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 83.3% vs 83.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Deebo Samuel Sr. 15+ receiving yds (79%) + George Pickens 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Christian McCaffrey 15+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 49.3%, fair +103. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 35.3% vs 35.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: CeeDee Lamb 80+ receiving yds (62%) + Dak Prescott 240+ passing yds (61%) + George Kittle 50+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 32.4%, fair +209. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.1% vs 14.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: George Pickens 10+ receiving yds (95%) + Javonte Williams 30+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 87.9%, fair -725. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 83.3% vs 83.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Deebo Samuel Sr. 15+ receiving yds (79%) + George Pickens 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Christian McCaffrey 15+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 49.3%, fair +103. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 35.3% vs 35.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: CeeDee Lamb 80+ receiving yds (62%) + Dak Prescott 240+ passing yds (61%) + George Kittle 50+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 32.4%, fair +209. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 20.1% vs 14.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Thursday; Kyle Shanahan called him 'real close' (ESPN, citing David Lombardi, Nov 13). Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited, and Brandon Aiyuk is on a roster exemption and out. Keenan Allen was acquired Nov 10 and has no role history with San Francisco (ESPN). Sunday update: Mike Evans (Achilles) is RULED OUT; Deebo Samuel Sr. has no designation; Keenan Allen will play (ESPN, Nick Wagoner and David Lombardi, Nov 13). LT Trent Williams's Friday questionable tag is no longer among ESPN's latest items; unconfirmed.

Tyler Goodson (ACL/MCL sprains) and Jake Ferguson (knee) are out (ESPN, citing Todd Archer and the Cowboys' site, Nov 9-10). George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) were limited Thursday and Jonathan Mingo (ankle/foot) did not practice (ESPN, citing Jon Machota, Nov 12-13). Sunday update: Tyler Goodson went on IR Saturday; Jonathan Mingo (ankle/foot) is RULED OUT. George Pickens and KaVontae Turpin have no designation and will play (ESPN, citing Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' site, Nov 13-14). RB Israel Abanikanda was elevated and TE James Mitchell signed. CBs DaRon Bland and Joey Porter Jr. (ankles) are questionable but expected to play (ESPN, citing Ian Rapoport, Nov 15).

Key injuries and uncertainties: Trent Williams (OT, Questionable); Renardo Green (CB, Questionable); Joey Porter Jr. (CB, Questionable); DaRon Bland (CB, Questionable); Jonathan Bullard (DT, Questionable); Donovan Ezeiruaku (LB, Out).

Does the line matchup predict? Pressure: yes Passing yards: no edge

Rebuilt game by game from data before each game, 562 team-games (2025 wk 5-18, 2026 wk 4-8).

Matchup callTeam-gamesExpected pressureActual pressureActual sack rateQB yds vs modelReceiving yds vs model
Line favored18817.4%19.4%5.8%+4.9+21.8
Even18721.2%21.9%6.3%-0.2+20.9
Rush favored18725.0%24.5%7.5%+1.0+18.9

The matchup does forecast pressure: correlation 0.20 with the pressure that happened (90% range 0.14 to 0.27), better than the line alone (0.13) or the rush alone (0.15). Rush-favored games had more sacks. But it did not predict passing yards beyond the model: correlation with QB yards minus projection -0.04 (90% range -0.10 to +0.03), with receiving yards -0.03. (Every row beat the model on receiving yards by a similar amount, a general lean in those backtest weeks; the gap between rows is what would show a line effect, and it is small.) Use it to judge sacks, hurried throws and whether a QB has time, not to move a yardage pick on its own.

Before kickoff

  1. Inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff. Rerun the slate after they do, and drop any pick whose player or key teammate is out.
  2. Questionable or doubtful: Derrick Harmon (DT, Questionable), Pat Freiermuth (TE, Questionable).
  3. Confirm the starting QBs: Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow. A change moves every passing and receiving line.
  4. Check the line has not moved past the minimum price shown. If it has, skip the pick rather than chase it.
  5. Check the kickoff forecast for 15+ mph wind or heavy rain. The market total usually moves first; if it drops 3+ points, rerun.

Building a parlay

  • Two or three legs. Each extra leg multiplies the risk: three 75% legs land together only about 42% of the time if independent.
  • Each leg at 70% or better from the Most likely tier, and no questionable players or QB-change teams.
  • Use the joint estimate, not the product. Same-game legs move together. A QB yardage over and his WR1 over are positively correlated; two receivers on one team partly compete for the same targets.
  • Price check: a parlay is worth taking only if its payout beats the fair odds of the joint estimate.

Conservative: Chase Brown 15+ rushing yds (93%) + DK Metcalf 15+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 82.4%, fair -467. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.6% vs 75.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Joe Burrow 220+ passing yds (79%) + Aaron Rodgers 180+ passing yds (78%) + DK Metcalf 25+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.5%, fair -120. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.8% vs 37.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Joe Burrow 260+ passing yds (61%) + Samaje Perine 19+ rushing yds (61%) + Darnell Washington 15+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 23.9%, fair +318. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.1% vs 17.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive breaks the 70% rule on purpose, for comparison.

Ranked by the calibrated model chance after the red-zone matchup is applied, so a receiver who draws a big share of red-zone targets against a defense that leaks red-zone passing TDs can rank above a running back. The model chance is calibrated. The matchup adjustment was backtested on 5,922 past forecasts (2025 and the 2026 holdout) and did not improve them: players it marked down still scored at or above the model's rate, and its top 5 hit no more often than the model's. Read it as context, not as an edge. Defensive rates are blended with 40 plays of league average to keep small samples from swinging it. Players listed Out, Doubtful or IR are excluded.

Player main lines
Lines are real DraftKings numbers, but ESPN's feed has no prop prices. Edge assumes -110 and is not a verified EV. Shrunk side first removes the slate-wide tilt in that market, then pulls our probability halfway to the line (log-odds), because we cannot prove the model beats the prop market. Min odds is the worst price worth taking, with a 2-point cushion. Check role marks a median more than 33% from the line, or a 20-point snap swing in the latest game. Either usually means usage history lags a real role change, so we do not count it as an edge.

Conservative, balanced, aggressive

Conservative: Chase Brown 15+ rushing yds (93%) + DK Metcalf 15+ receiving yds (89%). Joint estimate 82.4%, fair -467. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 75.6% vs 75.6% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Joe Burrow 220+ passing yds (79%) + Aaron Rodgers 180+ passing yds (78%) + DK Metcalf 25+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 54.5%, fair -120. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 41.8% vs 37.0% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Joe Burrow 260+ passing yds (61%) + Samaje Perine 19+ rushing yds (61%) + Darnell Washington 15+ receiving yds (61%). Joint estimate 23.9%, fair +318. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 18.1% vs 17.3% if independent. Not guaranteed.
